chunks: Abu al-Qasim ibn Qulawayh from his father from Ahmad ibn Idris said: He narrated to me Muhammad ibn Hamdan al-Kufi who said: He narrated to me al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sam'ah from Muhammad ibn Ziyad from 'Umarah ibn Marwan from Zayd al-Shahham who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "To be given a sa' of dates is more beloved to me than to be given a sa' of gold for the Fitrah (alms of fasting)."

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah, a common title for Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him).
key_terms.الْفِطْرَة: Fitrah, the obligatory alms-giving at the end of Ramadan (Zakat al-Fitr).
key_terms.تَمْر: Dates, the fruit of the date palm.
key_terms.صَاع: A traditional unit of volume measurement for dry goods, approximately 3-4 liters.

ai.seo_question: What is the preferred form of payment for Fitrah according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) prioritizes a *sa'* of dates over gold for Fitrah, emphasizing the prophetic tradition of distributing staple food to directly nourish the poor. This preference underscores the spiritual merit of tangible sustenance over abstract monetary value, reflecting the Shia scholarly view that Fitrah is fundamentally an act of feeding the needy rather than a mere tax.
